headline: High risk of cascading error and capability conflict: gpt-engineer can write/run code in a shared project directory while awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable knowledge list with no isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runnable I/O surfaces and is a knowledge-management list, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs. B writes files in a project directory and can read filesystem content, so a manual copy-paste or file-based bridge is possible, but the pathway is unusual and the blast radius is limited to prompt contamination rather than direct execution.
conditions: IF an operator copies B-generated text into A’s curation workflow, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF A is extended to parse B-written files as instructions, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Review any B-generated text before reusing it in A.
Do not auto-ingest files from B into A.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network surfaces, while B reads and writes a user-specified project directory and can call external model APIs. The pair does not show a shared workspace by default, so leakage is not inherent; if a shared directory contains secrets, B could transmit them to its backend.
conditions: IF the project directory contains secrets or regulated data, B can read them.
IF B is pointed at a shared workspace used by A, file contents may flow to B's model backend.
mitigations: Use a clean project directory for B.
Remove secrets from any shared folder.
Restrict B to non-sensitive files only.
Check that no credentials are present before running B.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation between agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has unrestricted filesystem write and per-project shared state via the project directory, while A is non-runnable and has no write surface. There is no direct write-write conflict, but if both are pointed at the same directory, B can overwrite or reorder artifacts that A treats as reference material, creating a default shared-state conflict even though A itself cannot write.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to use the same project directory, B can clobber shared artifacts.
IF A is used as a source-of-truth index for files B edits, stale references can arise.
mitigations: Assign separate directories to each agent.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same project tree.
Snapshot the directory before running B.
Check diffs after each B run.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared project state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s tool-use pattern is to write files and then offer to run code, so if A’s curated content or recommendations are fed into B as authoritative guidance, B can turn that into executable changes. A is a static knowledge list, but its outputs can still be treated as facts by B; the resulting blast radius includes code changes and execution under the user’s privileges.
conditions: IF A-derived recommendations are pasted into B as trusted requirements, B may implement them without verification.
IF B is allowed to run generated code, erroneous A-derived guidance can become executed changes.
mitigations: Verify A-derived claims before handing them to B.
Require human review before B runs generated code.
Limit B to file generation only.
Compare outputs against source docs.
requires-engineering: add a verification gate between A and B.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source knowledge-management site with no touched data classes, while B handles generated source code and may use OpenAI or another configured model. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented in the profiles, so only a small compliance risk exists if sensitive code or secrets are placed into B’s project directory and then sent to its backend.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are placed into B's workspace, external API transmission may create a policy mismatch.
IF A is used to curate compliance-sensitive content, no residency controls are documented for that workflow.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B.
Use redacted examples only.
Confirm the configured model provider's policy.
Document retention expectations before use.
requires-engineering: add data-class routing controls.
